newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Paranagua port starts sugar loading.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Paranagua port starts sugar loading.

text.p: The first sugar vessel has begun loading in Brazil's port of Paranagua, taking on the first of the 260,000 long tons of Paranagua raws delivered against the New York May contract, traders and port officials said.
The vessel, the Kay, has already loaded 2,400 tonnes out of a total of 14,000 tonnes in big bags, a port official said.
Another four vessels are waiting in the day, also to load sugar in "big bags" while two more are waiting to load sugar in bulk, he added.
Between May 9-11, a total of 377 trucks arrived at the port with sugar, bringing the total so far to 539 trucks, a port authority spokeswoman said.
"From this week, we are expecting to see around 250 trucks arriving a day," she said. Each truck carries between 25 to 30 tonnes, she estimated.
So far the port had 15,092 tonnes of sugar in warehouses, she added.
A total of 339,950 long tons were delivered against the May contract. In addition to the Paranagua raws, the balance was made up from north Brazil and three Central American nations.
U.S. trade house Cargill was the receiver of all the sugar.
Given Brazil's reputation for port delays, there has been speculation over whether Paranagua can handle such a quantity of sugar while it is also handling soycomplex exports.
Under contract rules, the sugar must be shipped by July 15, traders said.

Port officials estimated that if five gangways were used at a normal dock, a maximum of 2,000 tonnes of bulk sugar could be loaded per ship per day by slitting the "big bags" of one tonne at the hold.
The one bulk terminal believed to be ready to take sugar ships could possibly see a loading rate of 300 to 400 tonnes an hour, they added.

There had been talk a deal had been agreed with Eximcoop's bulk loading facility at the port but the terminal was still loading soybean products and would only likely be ready for sugar in the middle of June, an official said.
The terminal which last year saw exports of 285,000 tonnes of bulk sugar is expected to handle between 350,000 and 400,000 tonnes this year.

In total last calendar year, the port handled around one million tonnes of bulk and bagged sugar. In May to July, bagged and bulk sugar exports from the port were 132,262 and 119,483 tonnes respectively.
This year the port has already impressed soybean traders with its handling of soybean exports, expected to reach record levels in 1997.
To May 7, the port had shipped 2.01 million tonnes of soybeans against 923,351 tonnes in the same period last year and total 1996 soybean exports of 1.95 million tonnes.
This is not the first time Brazil has been the center of attention for New York May deliveries.
In May 1995, the center-south's main sugar port of Santos struggled to cope with record deliveries of around 510,000 tonnes Brazilian raws against the New York contract.
This year no sugar ships have so far arrived at Santos, nor has the port received any notification of when the first sugar ship is due to arrive, a port authority spokeswoman said.

The other question surrounding the deliveries is how exports can go ahead when traders are still awaiting the publication of a government notice reducing to zero the tax on sugar earmarked for export in the government's crop plan.
The Industry and Commerce Ministry passed the note to the Finance Ministry for approval at the same time as the crop plan, an Industry and Commerce Ministry official said.
A Finance Ministry official said the minister had received the note and that the approval should come soon.

In the meantime, the producer involved is said to have paid the equivalent of the export tax to allow shipments to begin on the understanding the money will be returned once the note is published, traders said.
((-Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
